summary: Changes safeGit to return a { code, stdout, stderr } object instead of a stdout string, and stops it throwing on a failing git command. Exports the new GitResult type from the core package entry.

findings.title: Return shape change breaks both CLI callers
findings.problem: safeGit now resolves to an object, but currentBranch at branch.ts:7 and changedFiles at status.ts:7 still treat it as a string. Neither caller is updated in this change.
findings.consequence: changedFiles throws a TypeError on out.split for every run, so main.ts crashes. currentBranch catches its TypeError and returns null, so main.ts reports not a git repository inside every repository.
findings.fix: Update both callers to read result.stdout, and check result.code where the old throw was relied on. Alternatively keep the string return and add the structured variant as a new function.

findings.title: Swallowed git failure defeats the null check in currentBranch
findings.problem: safeGit no longer throws on a failing command. currentBranch in packages/cli/src/branch.ts:5 relies on that throw to return null outside a repository.
findings.consequence: Once the callers read stdout, currentBranch returns an empty string instead of null outside a repository. main.ts then skips its not a git repository exit and runs changedFiles against a non-repository.
findings.fix: Have callers check result.code and treat a non-zero code as failure. Alternatively keep a throwing variant for callers that depend on the exception.

findings.title: New error path and return shape have no covering test
findings.problem: safeGit gains a new return shape and a catch branch that maps a thrown error to a code. The repository contains no test files that exercise safeGit.
findings.consequence: A regression in the code mapping or in the stdout fallback goes unnoticed until a CLI user hits it.
findings.fix: Add a test that runs safeGit in a temporary directory with a succeeding and a failing command. Assert code, stdout and stderr for both.
